quizzes.title: Status and Powers of the Election Commission
quizzes.passage: The Election Commission of India is a permanent, all-India and independent body that conducts elections across the country. Its basic task is to ensure that elections to the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies are free and fair, and it also oversees the elections of the President and the Vice President. Since 1993, the Commission has been a three-member body. It consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners, who together carry out its work. The Commission shares responsibility for electoral rolls with the state chief electoral officers and state election commissions. An electoral roll is the official list of people eligible to vote in a given election within a specific area, and being on that list is a legal requirement for casting a vote. Its work involves preparing voter lists and managing polls, and it also has functions that the Constitution and the courts have helped to define. Because its powers are rooted in the Constitution, the Commission is described as a constitutional body. Its members also enjoy fixed service conditions that cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment. The Commission's responsibilities cover the whole country, including every state and union territory.

questions.q: Under which power does the ECI resolve disputes over party recognition and allocate election symbols?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists party recognition disputes and symbol allocation under the quasi-judicial power of the ECI.

questions.q: In which situation can the ECI order a re-poll?
options: Only when a court disqualifies a candidate
When a State Legislature amends the election law
When voter turnout falls below half the electorate
When the purity of the electoral process is compromised
questions.explanation: The booklet says the ECI can order a re-poll if it believes the purity of the electoral process has been compromised.

questions.q: When does judicial review of the ECI's decisions usually take place?
options: Before the poll schedule is announced
questions.explanation: Judicial review of ECI actions usually comes after the election process so as not to disrupt the conduct of elections.

questions.q:
Read the statements below.
Assertion (A): The ECI can act independently to safeguard free and fair elections where laws made by Parliament or State Legislatures are silent.
Reason (R): The scope of the ECI's powers under Articles 327 and 328 covers situations in which such laws are silent.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet ties the ECI's independent action where laws are silent to the scope of its powers under Articles 327 and 328, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ECI:
I. The advisory power of the ECI includes guiding the authorities during emergencies.
II. Judicial review of the ECI's actions generally takes place before the election process begins.
III. The principles of natural justice are applied in a flexible and pragmatic manner in electoral matters.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I and III match the booklet, while statement II reverses the timing of judicial review.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ECI:
I. The administrative power of the ECI covers scheduling elections.
II. The advisory power of the ECI covers resolving disputes over party recognition.
III. The advisory power of the ECI covers advising the President and Governors.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II describes the quasi-judicial power instead.

questions.q: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body under which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The booklet places the ECI under Articles 324 to 329, which form Part XV of the Constitution.

questions.q: A CEC or EC serves for six years or until what age, whichever is earlier? (number)
questions.explanation: The tenure of the CEC and ECs is six years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: The CEC and ECs enjoy salary and status equal to a judge of which court? (name of the court)
questions.explanation: The CEC and ECs have equal status, rank and salary as a judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Which power of the ECI covers allocating election symbols? (name the power)
questions.explanation: Allocating election symbols falls under the quasi-judicial power of the ECI.

questions.q: Which power of the ECI covers defining constituencies? (name the power)
questions.explanation: Defining constituencies is one of the ECI's administrative powers.

questions.q: Which legal principle does the Supreme Court say is applied in a flexible and pragmatic manner in electoral matters? (two words)
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court emphasised a flexible and pragmatic application of the principles of natural justice in electoral contexts.

questions.q: In which year was the Election Commission of India established? (year)
questions.explanation: The ECI was founded on 25 January 1950.

questions.q: Can a CEC who has completed a term be re-appointed? (answer yes or no)
questions.explanation: The CEC and ECs are not eligible for re-appointment.

quizzes.title: The EVM and the VVPAT
quizzes.passage: The Electronic Voting Machine, known as the EVM, is an electronic device that records votes in place of the traditional ballot papers and ballot boxes. The machine has been used in elections to the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and by-elections, and it has been in use across different parts of the country for several decades. Since it is electronic, votes are stored in the machine rather than being collected and counted manually from paper. A companion system, the Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail, is attached to the EVM and is meant to give voters a way to check their choice. When a vote is cast, a paper slip is generated, and the slip lets the voter see the choice made before it is stored. The system is described as an independent unit that works alongside the EVM. The purpose of this arrangement is to increase confidence in the voting process among voters and political parties alike. Courts have also commented on the role of such systems in elections, and several judgments have discussed them. The overall aim is to make the physical record of each vote available for verification. Its use expanded gradually over the following years, and it was extended to elections across the country.

questions.q: Which Assembly constituency first used EVMs in 1982?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that EVMs were first used in the Paravur Assembly Constituency of Kerala in 1982.

questions.q: For how many seconds does the VVPAT slip remain visible through the transparent window?
questions.explanation: The slip stays exposed through the transparent window for 7 seconds before it is cut and falls into the sealed drop box.

questions.q: Along with Electronic Corporation of India Ltd, which company developed the EVM?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the EVM was developed by Bharat Electronics Ltd (Bangalore) and Electronic Corporation of India Ltd (Hyderabad).

questions.q:
Read the statements below.
Assertion (A): The VVPAT allows voters to verify that their votes are cast as intended.
Reason (R): The VVPAT prints a slip showing the serial number, candidate name and symbol, which the voter can see before it is stored.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The printed slip is the means by which voters verify their vote, so R correctly explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Control Unit   ->   A. Kept with the Polling Officer
II. Balloting Unit   ->   B. Placed in the voting booth
III. VVPAT slip visibility   ->   C. Seven seconds
IV. Noksen Assembly bye-election   ->   D. First VVPAT use (2013)
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: The booklet places the Control Unit with the Polling Officer, the Balloting Unit in the booth, and VVPAT was first introduced in the Noksen bye-election in 2013.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the EVM and VVPAT:
I. The VVPAT machines can be accessed by Polling Officers only.
II. The Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended to allow a printer with a drop box to be attached to the EVM.
III. The EVM was first used in Kerala in 1989.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III gives the wrong year, as the EVM was first used in Kerala in 1982.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the EVM and VVPAT:
I. The EVM records votes in place of ballot papers and boxes.
II. The VVPAT slip remains visible for 10 seconds before it falls into the drop box.
III. EVMs were adopted for general elections in 2004.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II gives 10 seconds instead of the 7 seconds stated in the booklet.

questions.q: In which year was VVPAT first introduced, in the Noksen bye-election in Nagaland? (year)
questions.explanation: VVPAT was first introduced in the Noksen Assembly bye-election of Nagaland in 2013.

questions.q: After the 2019 Supreme Court ruling, how many EVMs' VVPAT slips per constituency must be counted? (number)
questions.explanation: The 2019 ruling required VVPAT slips of 5 EVMs in every constituency to be counted instead of 1.

questions.q: In which year were VVPATs used in all constituencies of the Lok Sabha elections? (year)
questions.explanation: VVPATs were used in all constituencies in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections.

questions.q: The Representation of the People Act, of which year, was amended in 1989 to permit EVM use? (year)
questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 was amended in 1989 to permit EVM use.

questions.q: Which model of EVM and VVPAT is presently used? (model name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the M3 model of EVM and VVPAT is presently used.

questions.q: In which city is Electronic Corporation of India Ltd based? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Electronic Corporation of India Ltd as based in Hyderabad.

questions.q: In which year was VVPAT first proposed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the VVPAT was initially proposed in 2010 and approved by the ECI in 2013.
